cases.title: Search URLBar text via search button
cases.description: Enter valid text into the URLBar and click the search button to ensure the search is executed correctly.

cases.title: Display search results in sidebar search tab
cases.description: Initiate a search from the URL bar and verify that the results are displayed in the sidebar search tab.

cases.title: Start search from within sidebar search tab
cases.description: Perform a search action directly from the sidebar search tab and verify it executes successfully.

cases.title: Change the active search engine
cases.description: Select an alternative search engine from the available list and verify that subsequent searches use the new engine.

cases.title: Bookmark a conducted search
cases.description: Execute a search and verify that the conducted search is successfully bookmarked.

opinions.feedback: The proposed high-level test cases are clear, distinct, cover all requirements properly, and are fully testable without any blockers.
All test cases and expected behaviors accurately map to the provided requirements without any blockers.

analysis.analysis: R-135: Testable behavior is clicking the search button to trigger a search of URLBar text; normal path is entering valid text and clicking the button, abnormal path is clicking with empty URLBar; boundary is maximum length of URLBar text; ambiguity is whether pressing 'Enter' counts as clicking the button. R-136: Testable behavior is displaying search results in the sidebar search tab upon starting a URL bar search; normal path is results appearing correctly, abnormal path is sidebar closed or failing to load; boundary is empty search results; ambiguity is definition of 'starting' a search. R-137: Testable behavior is initiating a search directly from the sidebar search tab; normal path is typing and executing search within the sidebar, abnormal path is input validation failure; boundary is handling special characters; ambiguity is whether it uses the default engine. R-138: Testable behavior is changing the search engine; normal path is selecting an alternative engine from a list, abnormal path is selecting an invalid or removed engine; boundary is switching between maximum number of supported engines; ambiguity is whether the change applies globally or per-tab. R-139: Testable behavior is bookmarking a conducted search automatically or via prompt; normal path is successful bookmark creation, abnormal path is duplicate bookmark or storage failure; boundary is maximum bookmarks limit; ambiguity is whether bookmarking is automatic for all searches or user-triggered.
